title: A Small Garden at School
passage: Mika's class had a small empty space behind the science room. In April, their teacher asked, "What can we do with this place?" The students decided to make a garden. They planted tomatoes, beans, and sunflowers. Mika watered the plants every morning before class. At first, the plants were very small, and some students thought nothing would grow. In June, however, the garden became green and bright. The class picked tomatoes and used them in a simple lunch. Mika was happy because the garden was made by everyone. She learned that a small place can change when people work together.
translation: ミカのクラスには、理科室の後ろに小さな空きスペースがありました。4月、先生が「この場所で何ができるかな」と尋ねました。生徒たちは庭を作ることにし、トマト、豆、ひまわりを植えました。ミカは毎朝、授業前に植物へ水をやりました。最初はとても小さく、何も育たないと思う生徒もいました。しかし6月には庭は緑で明るくなりました。クラスはトマトを収穫し、簡単な昼食に使いました。ミカは、みんなで作った庭なのでうれしく思いました。そして、小さな場所でも人々が協力すれば変えられることを学びました。

questions.question: Where was the empty space?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says the space was behind the science room.

questions.question: What did Mika do every morning?
questions.explanation: Mika watered the plants every morning before class.

questions.question: What happened in June?
choices: The garden became green and bright
questions.explanation: The passage directly states that the garden became green and bright in June.

questions.question: Why was Mika happy?
choices: Everyone had made the garden together
questions.explanation: Mika was happy because the garden was made by everyone.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
choices: Working together can improve a small place
Students should arrive early every day
questions.explanation: The ending emphasizes that a place can change when people work together.

title: The Wallet on the Bench
passage: Ken was waiting for a train after soccer practice. He sat on a bench and saw a brown wallet beside him. He opened it only to look for a name. There was an identification card inside, but there was no phone number. Ken took the wallet to the station office. Ten minutes later, an older man came in quickly. He looked worried and asked about a lost wallet. The station worker asked his name and checked the card. Then she returned the wallet to him. The man thanked Ken many times. Ken almost missed his train, but he did not mind. On the way home, he felt that he had made the right choice.
translation: ケンはサッカーの練習後、電車を待っていました。ベンチに座ると、隣に茶色の財布があるのを見つけました。名前を確認するためだけに中を開けると、身分証明書はありましたが電話番号はありませんでした。ケンは財布を駅の窓口へ持っていきました。10分後、年配の男性が急いで入ってきました。男性は心配そうで、なくした財布について尋ねました。駅員は名前を聞いてカードを確認し、財布を返しました。男性は何度もケンにお礼を言いました。ケンは電車に乗り遅れそうになりましたが、気にしませんでした。帰り道、正しい選択をしたと感じました。

questions.explanation: Ken saw the wallet beside him on the bench.

questions.question: Why did Ken open the wallet?
questions.explanation: The passage says he opened it only to look for a name.

questions.question: Who came to the station office?
questions.explanation: An older man came in looking worried about his lost wallet.

choices: Proud of making the right choice
questions.explanation: He felt that he had made the right choice.

questions.question: Which title best fits the story?
choices: A Helpful Choice at the Station
questions.explanation: The story centers on Ken returning a lost wallet at the station.

title: A Rainy Day in the Library
passage: It rained heavily on Friday, so Aya could not practice tennis outside. She went to the school library instead. She planned to stay for only twenty minutes, but she found a book about famous bridges around the world. Aya liked the pictures and began reading about how bridges are built. One bridge had to be strong enough for trains, while another was designed for people and bicycles. Aya forgot about the rain and read for almost an hour. Before leaving, she borrowed the book. The next week, her class started a project about buildings. Aya smiled because she already had an idea for her project.
translation: 金曜日は雨が激しく降ったため、アヤは外でテニスの練習ができませんでした。代わりに学校の図書館へ行きました。20分だけいるつもりでしたが、世界の有名な橋についての本を見つけました。写真が気に入り、橋がどのように造られるかを読み始めました。ある橋は列車が通れるほど強くする必要があり、別の橋は人や自転車用に設計されていました。アヤは雨のことを忘れ、ほぼ1時間読みました。帰る前にその本を借りました。翌週、クラスで建物についての課題が始まり、アヤはすでに案があったので笑顔になりました。

Her teacher told her to go
She wanted to meet a friend
questions.explanation: Heavy rain prevented outdoor tennis practice.

questions.explanation: Aya found a book about famous bridges around the world.

questions.explanation: She planned to stay briefly but read for almost an hour.

choices: She already had a project idea

choices: Unexpected changes can lead to useful discoveries

Sports are more useful than books
questions.explanation: The canceled practice led Aya to discover a book that helped with a later project.

title: The Earlier Bus
passage: Riku usually took the 7:45 bus to school. One Monday, his mother asked him to take the 7:30 bus because she needed to leave home early. Riku did not like the idea because he wanted fifteen more minutes of sleep. However, when he arrived near school, he noticed a small bakery that he had never seen open before. The baker was putting fresh bread on a shelf by the window. Riku bought one roll and ate it in the park. The morning felt quiet and peaceful. After that day, Riku did not take the earlier bus every morning, but he sometimes chose it when he wanted a calm start to the day.
translation: リクはいつも7時45分のバスで学校へ行っていました。ある月曜日、母が早く家を出る必要があり、7時30分のバスに乗ってほしいと頼みました。リクはあと15分眠りたかったので、その案が好きではありませんでした。しかし学校の近くに着くと、これまで開いているのを見たことがない小さなパン屋に気づきました。パン職人が焼きたてのパンを窓際の棚に並べていました。リクはロールパンを1つ買い、公園で食べました。朝は静かで穏やかでした。その後、毎朝早いバスに乗るわけではありませんでしたが、落ち着いた一日の始まりがほしいときには時々選ぶようになりました。

questions.explanation: The first sentence says he usually took the 7:45 bus.

choices: He always took the early bus

He sometimes took it for a calm start
questions.explanation: He sometimes chose the earlier bus when he wanted a calm start.

title: The Bicycle Repair Club
passage: At Haru's school, many students came by bicycle. One day, Haru saw a student pushing a bicycle with a flat tire. He wanted to help but did not know how. That weekend, he watched his uncle repair a tire and asked many questions. Haru then had an idea: students could learn simple bicycle repairs together. A teacher helped him start a small after-school club. At first, only four students joined. They practiced fixing flat tires, adjusting seats, and checking brakes. Soon other students began bringing bicycles with small problems. The club did not repair dangerous damage; for that, they told students to visit a professional shop. By summer, twelve students were in the club. Haru was pleased that learning one useful skill had created a place where students could help one another.
translation: ハルの学校では多くの生徒が自転車で通っていました。ある日、ハルはタイヤがパンクした自転車を押している生徒を見ました。助けたかったのですが、直し方を知りませんでした。その週末、叔父がタイヤを修理するのを見て、たくさん質問しました。そして、生徒同士で簡単な自転車修理を学ぶクラブを作ることを思いつきました。先生の助けで放課後クラブを始め、最初は4人だけでした。パンク修理、サドル調整、ブレーキ確認を練習しました。やがて他の生徒も小さな故障の自転車を持ってくるようになりました。危険な損傷は直さず、専門店へ行くよう伝えました。夏までに部員は12人になりました。1つの役立つ技能を学んだことが、生徒同士で助け合う場所につながったことをハルは喜びました。

questions.explanation: Dangerous damage was left to professionals.

questions.explanation: The passage states that twelve students were in the club by summer.

choices: Useful skills can help build a supportive community
Students should repair all bicycle damage

questions.explanation: Haru's skill led to a club where students could help one another.

title: Reusable Cups at the Festival
passage: Every autumn, Midori Town holds a food festival in the central park. Last year, volunteers collected more than thirty large bags of trash after the event. Most of the trash was paper and plastic cups. This year, a group of high school students suggested using reusable cups. Visitors paid a small deposit when they bought a drink. When they returned the cup, they got the money back. Some shop owners worried that the system would be confusing, so the students made large signs and placed return boxes near every exit. At the end of the festival, the volunteers counted only twelve bags of trash. Washing the cups required extra work, but the organizers decided to use the system again. They also planned to improve the return boxes so that the next festival would be even easier for visitors.
translation: 毎年秋、緑町では中央公園で食の祭りが開かれます。昨年はイベント後、ボランティアが30袋以上のごみを集め、その多くは紙やプラスチックのカップでした。今年、高校生のグループが再利用できるカップを提案しました。来場者は飲み物を買うときに少額の預かり金を払い、カップを返すと返金されました。店主の中には仕組みが分かりにくいと心配する人もいたため、生徒たちは大きな案内を作り、各出口の近くに返却箱を置きました。祭りの終わりには、ごみは12袋だけでした。カップを洗う手間は増えましたが、主催者は来年もこの仕組みを使うことにしました。さらに返却箱を改善し、次回はもっと利用しやすくする予定です。

choices: It reduced trash despite extra washing work

questions.explanation: The organizers judged the waste reduction worth the extra work.

title: A Museum Guide for One Day
passage: Yuna's class visited a local history museum, but this time the students were not only visitors. Each student chose one object and prepared a short explanation for younger children. Yuna selected an old wooden lunch box used by workers about a hundred years ago. She first wrote a long explanation with many dates. During practice, however, her friend said it was difficult to follow. Yuna changed her plan. She asked the children to imagine carrying lunch without a refrigerator or a microwave, and then showed them the box. On the museum day, several children asked questions about the food people ate in the past. Yuna realized that a good guide does not simply give more information. A guide has to help listeners connect unfamiliar things with something they already understand.
translation: ユナのクラスは地域の歴史博物館を訪れましたが、今回は見学者になるだけではありませんでした。各生徒が展示物を1つ選び、年下の子ども向けに短い説明を準備しました。ユナは約100年前に働く人が使った古い木製の弁当箱を選びました。最初は年代をたくさん入れた長い説明を書きましたが、練習で友達に分かりにくいと言われました。そこで、冷蔵庫や電子レンジなしで昼食を持ち運ぶことを想像してもらい、その後で箱を見せる方法に変えました。当日、子どもたちは昔の食事についていくつも質問しました。ユナは、良い案内役は単に情報を増やすのではなく、知らないものをすでに知っていることと結びつける手助けをする必要があると気づきました。

choices: A short explanation of one object
questions.explanation: Each student chose an object and prepared an explanation.

questions.explanation: She connected the old lunch box with the familiar idea of carrying lunch today.

questions.explanation: Several children asked about food in the past.

questions.question: What did Yuna learn about explaining things?
choices: Listeners should already know the topic
Connections to familiar ideas can improve understanding
questions.explanation: The final sentence states that guides should connect unfamiliar ideas to things listeners understand.

title: Lunch with a New Classmate
passage: When Leo came to Japan as an exchange student, he understood classroom English well, but casual conversations were harder for him. At lunch, his classmates often spoke quickly and changed topics before he could answer. Mei noticed that Leo smiled but rarely joined in. The next day, she sat beside him and asked one question at a time. She also waited a little longer after asking. At first, the pauses felt unusual, but Leo began telling the group about his school and favorite music. Soon other students slowed down too. A week later, Leo was starting conversations himself. Mei had not taught him new grammar or vocabulary. Instead, she had changed the pace of the conversation, giving him enough time to use the language he already knew.
translation: レオが交換留学生として日本へ来たとき、授業で使う英語はよく理解できましたが、日常会話はもっと難しく感じました。昼食時、クラスメートは速く話し、レオが答える前に話題が変わることがよくありました。メイは、レオが笑顔ではいるものの会話にはほとんど加わらないことに気づきました。翌日、隣に座り、質問を一つずつして、質問後も少し長く待ちました。最初はその間が不自然に感じられましたが、レオは自分の学校や好きな音楽について話し始めました。ほかの生徒も話す速度を落とし、1週間後にはレオ自身が会話を始めるようになりました。メイは新しい文法や単語を教えたのではなく、会話の速度を変え、レオがすでに知っている言葉を使える時間を作ったのです。

questions.question: What did Mei notice?
questions.explanation: Mei noticed that he smiled but rarely joined in.

choices: The pace and timing of the conversation
questions.explanation: She asked one question at a time and waited longer.

questions.question: What was Leo doing a week later?
questions.explanation: A week later, Leo was starting conversations himself.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

How giving someone time can help communication
Why music is useful for language study
How to speak as quickly as possible
questions.explanation: The key change was providing enough time for Leo to participate.

title: The Weather Station on the Roof
passage: The science club at Nishi Junior High wanted to know why the schoolyard sometimes felt much hotter than the nearby park. Instead of relying only on a weather app, the students placed small temperature sensors in three locations: the roof, the schoolyard, and a shaded area beside several trees. They recorded the temperature every ten minutes for two weeks. At first, they expected the roof to be hottest all day. The data showed a more complicated pattern. Around noon, the roof was usually hottest, but in the late afternoon the schoolyard often remained warmer because its dark surface released heat slowly. The shaded area changed the least. The students presented the results to the school and suggested adding more shade near the benches. Their project did not prove that one change would solve the heat problem, but it showed them how measurements could turn a general feeling—"this place is hot"—into a question that could be studied.
translation: 西中学校の科学部は、校庭が近くの公園よりずっと暑く感じることがある理由を調べたいと考えました。天気アプリだけに頼らず、屋上、校庭、数本の木のそばの日陰の3か所に小型温度センサーを置き、2週間、10分ごとに気温を記録しました。最初は一日中屋上が最も暑いと予想しましたが、データはもっと複雑でした。正午ごろは屋上が最も暑いことが多い一方、夕方遅くには暗い地面が熱をゆっくり放出するため校庭の方が暖かいことがよくありました。日陰の場所は変化が最も小さくなりました。生徒たちは結果を学校に発表し、ベンチ周辺に日陰を増やすことを提案しました。この研究だけで一つの対策が暑さ問題を解決すると証明したわけではありませんが、「ここは暑い」という感覚を、測定によって調べられる問いに変えられることを学びました。

questions.question: Why did the students use their own sensors?
choices: They wanted measurements from specific school locations
Weather apps were forbidden at school
They wanted to predict rain for sports day
questions.explanation: They wanted location-specific measurements rather than relying only on a general weather app.

questions.question: What surprised the students about the schoolyard?
choices: It was always colder than the shade
It often stayed warmer late in the afternoon
It had the highest temperature every morning
questions.explanation: The dark surface released stored heat slowly, keeping the yard warmer later.

questions.question: Which location changed the least?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says the shaded area changed the least.

questions.question: What does 'a more complicated pattern' mean here?
choices: Different places were hottest at different times
The students could not read the numbers
All locations had exactly the same temperature
questions.explanation: The hottest location depended on the time of day.

questions.question: What larger lesson did the students learn?
choices: Measurements can turn impressions into testable questions
One experiment always proves a final solution
Roofs should never be used for science
questions.explanation: The final sentence states this broader lesson directly.

title: The Walking Map Project
passage: A city tourism office asked local students to create a digital walking map for visitors. The first group chose the shortest route between the station and an old temple. When they tested it, however, they discovered that the route included a narrow road with heavy traffic and almost no sidewalk. A second route was seven minutes longer but passed a river, a small shopping street, and two public restrooms. The students interviewed visitors and found that most preferred the longer route because it felt safer and more interesting. This changed the way the students thought about maps. A map is not only a tool for finding the shortest distance. It can also reflect what users value, such as safety, scenery, rest areas, or accessibility. In the final version, the map offered three routes—fast, scenic, and step-free—instead of recommending a single "best" route for everyone.
translation: 市の観光課が地域の生徒に、旅行者向けのデジタル散策マップ作りを依頼しました。最初のグループは駅から古い寺まで最短の道を選びましたが、実際に歩くと交通量が多く歩道がほとんどない細い道路を通ることが分かりました。2つ目の道は7分長いものの、川、小さな商店街、2か所の公衆トイレを通りました。旅行者に聞くと、多くの人が安全で面白いと感じる長い道を好みました。これにより、生徒たちは地図についての考えを変えました。地図は最短距離を探すだけの道具ではなく、安全、景色、休憩場所、利用しやすさなど、利用者が大切にすることも反映できます。最終版では一つの「最良ルート」を勧めるのではなく、速い道、景色のよい道、段差のない道の3種類を提示しました。

questions.question: What problem did the shortest route have?
choices: It used a narrow road with heavy traffic
questions.explanation: The shortest route lacked a safe sidewalk and had heavy traffic.

questions.question: Why did most visitors prefer the second route?
choices: It felt safer and more interesting
It ended at a different temple
questions.explanation: Visitors valued safety and interest more than saving seven minutes.

questions.question: What did the students realize about maps?
choices: Maps should always show one route
Distance is the only important factor
Maps can reflect different user needs

questions.explanation: The passage says maps can reflect values such as safety and accessibility.

questions.question: What does 'step-free' most likely mean?
choices: A route without stairs or steps
A route that requires no walking
A route used only at night
questions.explanation: In an accessibility context, step-free means avoiding stairs or steps.

questions.question: Why did the final map offer three routes?
choices: The city required exactly three routes
The students could not choose a destination
questions.explanation: The project showed that there is not one best route for every user.

title: What the Beach Cleanup Revealed
passage: Students from a coastal town joined a monthly beach cleanup. During the first few events, they simply counted the number of trash bags they filled. The total was useful, but it did not tell them where the trash came from. Their science teacher suggested recording each type of item before throwing it away. Over three months, the students found many drink containers after weekends, but they also found hundreds of small plastic pieces that were difficult to identify. Fishing line appeared mostly near the northern end of the beach, while food wrappers were common near the parking area. The students shared these patterns with local groups. As a result, new collection boxes for fishing line were placed near the northern entrance, and clearer signs were added near the parking area. The students still cleaned the beach, but their goal changed: they wanted not only to remove waste, but also to understand it well enough to reduce future waste.
translation: 海辺の町の生徒たちは毎月の海岸清掃に参加しました。最初の数回は集めたごみ袋の数だけを数えていました。総量は役立つ情報でしたが、ごみがどこから来たかまでは分かりません。理科の先生が、捨てる前にごみの種類ごとに記録することを提案しました。3か月で、週末の後には飲料容器が多く、正体を特定しにくい小さなプラスチック片も何百個も見つかりました。釣り糸は海岸北側に多く、食品包装は駐車場付近に多くありました。生徒たちはこの傾向を地域団体と共有しました。その結果、北側入口付近に釣り糸回収箱が設置され、駐車場近くには分かりやすい案内が追加されました。生徒たちは清掃を続けましたが、目的はごみを取るだけでなく、将来のごみを減らせるほど理解することへ変わりました。

questions.question: Why was counting only trash bags not enough?
choices: It did not show the sources or types of waste
questions.explanation: The total amount did not reveal where the waste came from.

questions.question: Where was fishing line found most often?
questions.explanation: Fishing line appeared mostly near the northern end.

questions.question: What action followed the students' findings?
choices: Special fishing-line boxes and clearer signs were added
questions.explanation: Local groups used the patterns to place targeted collection boxes and signs.

questions.question: How did the students' goal change?
choices: From cleaning to understanding and prevention as well
From monthly work to daily work
questions.explanation: They continued cleaning but also tried to reduce future waste.

questions.question: What is the best summary?
choices: Detailed data can help turn cleanup into prevention
All beach trash comes from fishing
Counting bags is always the best research method
questions.explanation: The passage shows how classifying waste enabled more targeted prevention.

title: A Different Kind of Study Room
passage: A junior high school library had a problem. Some students wanted complete silence, while others wanted to discuss homework with friends. The library had only one large study room, and arguments became common. Instead of making one rule for the whole room, the librarian tried a two-week experiment. The front half became a silent zone, and quiet conversation was allowed in the back half. Simple signs showed the two areas. At the end of each day, students could place a colored sticker on a board to show whether the arrangement worked for them. Most responses were positive, but several students said sound from the discussion area still reached the silent side. In the second week, bookshelves were moved between the areas and the discussion tables were placed farther back. Complaints decreased. The librarian concluded that the important part of the experiment was not the first solution itself, but the process of observing how people actually used the space and adjusting the design.
translation: 中学校の図書館には問題がありました。完全な静けさを望む生徒と、友達と宿題を相談したい生徒がいたのです。大きな自習室は1つだけで、言い争いがよく起きました。図書館司書は全体に一つの規則を課す代わりに、2週間の実験をしました。前半分を静かな区域にし、後ろ半分では小声の会話を認め、簡単な表示を置きました。毎日の終わりに、生徒は色付きシールでこの配置が使いやすかったかを示しました。多くは肯定的でしたが、話し合い区域の音が静かな側まで届くという意見もありました。2週目には区域間に本棚を移し、話し合い机をさらに奥へ置いたところ、苦情が減りました。司書は、重要なのは最初の解決策そのものではなく、実際の使われ方を観察して設計を調整する過程だと結論づけました。

questions.question: What caused arguments in the study room?
choices: Students wanted different levels of quiet
questions.explanation: Some students wanted silence while others wanted to discuss homework.

questions.question: What did students use the stickers for?
choices: To show whether the arrangement worked for them
questions.explanation: The sticker board collected daily feedback about the new arrangement.

questions.question: Why were bookshelves moved?
choices: To make more room for new books
To reduce sound reaching the silent area
questions.explanation: The shelves helped separate the zones after students reported sound problems.

questions.question: What happened after the second change?
questions.explanation: Complaints decreased after the layout was adjusted.

questions.question: What did the librarian consider most important?
choices: Observing use and improving the design
Keeping the room silent at all times
Using as many signs as possible
questions.explanation: The conclusion emphasizes observation and adjustment rather than a perfect first solution.

title: Measuring Food Waste in the Cafeteria
passage: When a student council announced a campaign to reduce cafeteria waste, its first idea was simple: posters would tell students not to leave food. A teacher asked the council to measure the problem before choosing a solution. For five days, volunteers weighed uneaten food after lunch and recorded which dishes were left most often. They also conducted an anonymous survey. The results challenged several assumptions. Students were not mainly wasting desserts or vegetables; large portions of rice were the biggest source of waste. In the survey, many students said they wanted to finish their meals but could not choose a smaller serving when they were less hungry. The cafeteria then tested two rice portions for a month. Students could request a regular or small serving and take more later if needed. Total rice waste fell by 38 percent, while the number of students asking for extra rice remained low. The council still used posters, but their message changed. Instead of blaming students for waste, the posters explained the new serving choice. The project taught the council that behavior can be shaped by the options people are given, not only by what they are told to do.
translation: 生徒会が給食の食べ残しを減らす運動を発表したとき、最初の案は「残さないで」と呼びかけるポスターでした。先生は、解決策を決める前に問題を測るよう提案しました。5日間、ボランティアは昼食後の食べ残しを量り、どの料理がよく残るか記録し、匿名アンケートも行いました。結果は予想を覆しました。主なごみはデザートや野菜ではなく、大盛りのご飯でした。多くの生徒は食べ切りたいが、空腹でないときも小盛りを選べないと答えました。そこで食堂は1か月、普通盛りと小盛りを選べ、必要なら後で追加できる方式を試しました。ご飯の廃棄は38％減り、おかわりを求める生徒は少数でした。生徒会はポスターも使いましたが、非難する内容ではなく新しい盛り方を知らせる内容に変えました。この活動から、行動は「何をしなさい」と言われることだけでなく、用意された選択肢によっても変わると学びました。

questions.question: Why did the teacher ask students to measure waste first?
choices: To understand the actual problem before choosing a solution
To decide which posters looked best
questions.explanation: The teacher wanted evidence about the problem before intervention.

questions.question: Which finding challenged the students' assumptions?
choices: Large rice portions caused the most waste
questions.explanation: Rice, not the expected foods, was the biggest source of waste.

questions.question: What change did the cafeteria test?
choices: Offering regular or small portions with extra available later
questions.explanation: The intervention changed portion choice while preserving access to more rice.

questions.question: Why did the poster message change?
choices: The council stopped caring about waste
The solution focused on informing students about a useful choice rather than blaming them
The cafeteria banned posters about food
questions.explanation: The new message supported the redesigned choice system.

questions.question: What broader conclusion does the passage support?
choices: People's behavior depends partly on how choices are structured
Students always choose the smallest portion
Surveys are more important than measurements
questions.explanation: The final sentence states that options can shape behavior, not only instructions.

title: The Timetable Survey
passage: A regional railway company planned to revise its evening timetable. Passenger counts showed that the 6:10 train was crowded, so the company considered adding another train shortly afterward. Before making the change, however, it asked a local university team to study how passengers actually used the line. The researchers combined ticket-gate data with short interviews at three stations. They discovered that many passengers on the 6:10 train were students transferring from buses that arrived only a few minutes earlier. A new 6:20 train would therefore do little to reduce crowding, because most of those students would still board the first train they could catch. The researchers proposed a different idea: move the 6:10 departure to 6:14 and coordinate one bus route so that passengers were divided between two existing trains. A one-month trial reduced the average number of standing passengers without adding a new train. The case showed why counts alone can describe where congestion occurs but may not explain the timing and connections that create it.
translation: 地域の鉄道会社は夕方の時刻表改定を計画していました。乗客数から6時10分の列車が混雑していることが分かり、その直後に列車を増発する案が出ました。しかし変更前に、地域の大学チームへ利用実態の調査を依頼しました。研究者は改札データと3駅での短い聞き取りを組み合わせ、多くの6時10分利用者が数分前に到着するバスから乗り換える学生だと分かりました。そのため6時20分に新列車を加えても、生徒は最初に乗れる列車に乗るので混雑解消効果は小さいと考えられました。研究者は別案として、6時10分発を6時14分へずらし、1つのバス路線を調整して既存の2本へ乗客を分散させました。1か月の試行で、列車を増やさず立っている乗客の平均人数が減りました。この事例は、人数データだけでは混雑場所は分かっても、その原因となる時間や乗り継ぎまでは説明できないことを示しました。

questions.question: Why did the company first consider adding a train?
choices: Passengers requested a later morning train
questions.explanation: Passenger counts showed heavy crowding on the 6:10 service.

questions.question: What did interviews reveal?
choices: Many students arrived from buses just before 6:10
questions.explanation: The transfer timing explained why students concentrated on the 6:10 train.

questions.question: Why might a new 6:20 train have had limited effect?
choices: Students would still take the first train available
The station could not display it
questions.explanation: The students' arrival pattern made them likely to board the earlier train anyway.

questions.question: What was unusual about the successful trial?
choices: It reduced crowding without adding a train
questions.explanation: Coordination and a small timetable shift improved crowding using existing trains.

questions.question: What is the author's main point?
choices: Crowding can be understood from counts alone
Understanding connections and behavior can change the best solution
Interviews are always more accurate than data
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts descriptive counts with information about the causes of the pattern.

title: Listening for Migrating Birds
passage: Every spring, thousands of birds migrate across a large lake at night. Because darkness makes visual counting difficult, a group of researchers invited local residents to help collect another kind of evidence: sound. Volunteers placed small audio recorders in gardens and fields around the lake. The devices recorded short samples throughout the night, and software marked sections that might contain bird calls. Human volunteers then listened to those sections and identified species when possible. The system was not fully automatic. Wind, frogs, and distant traffic often produced sounds that the software incorrectly marked as birds. Yet the combination of software and human checking allowed the team to examine far more hours of audio than people could review alone. After two seasons, the researchers found that some species passed the eastern shore earlier in the spring than expected. They are now comparing this pattern with temperature and insect data. The project illustrates a useful division of labor: computers can rapidly narrow a large amount of material, while people can apply context and judgment to uncertain cases.
translation: 毎年春、何千羽もの鳥が夜間に大きな湖を渡って移動します。暗闇では目で数えにくいため、研究者たちは地域住民に別の証拠、つまり音の収集を手伝ってもらいました。ボランティアは湖周辺の庭や野原に小型録音機を置き、夜間に短い音声を繰り返し記録しました。ソフトウェアが鳥の声かもしれない部分を印づけ、その部分を人が聞いて可能なら種を特定しました。完全自動ではなく、風、カエル、遠くの交通音を鳥と誤判定することも多くありました。それでもソフトウェアと人の確認を組み合わせることで、人だけでは確認できない大量の音声を調べられました。2シーズン後、一部の鳥が予想より早い春の時期に東岸を通ることが分かり、現在は気温や昆虫データとの関係を調べています。この研究は、コンピューターが大量資料を高速に絞り込み、人が不確かな例に文脈と判断を加えるという役割分担を示しています。

questions.question: Why did the project focus on sound?
choices: Audio equipment is always more accurate
Residents could not visit the lake
questions.explanation: Because migration occurs at night, visual observation is difficult.

questions.question: What was the software used for?
choices: To mark audio sections that might contain bird calls
questions.explanation: It narrowed the recordings to likely bird-call sections.

questions.question: What problem did the software have?
choices: It recorded only during the day
It sometimes marked non-bird sounds as birds
It could not process any audio
questions.explanation: Wind, frogs, and traffic created false positives.

questions.question: What new pattern did researchers notice?
choices: Some species passed the eastern shore earlier than expected
questions.explanation: The two-season data revealed earlier passage for some species.

questions.question: What idea does the project illustrate?
choices: Human and computer strengths can complement each other
Citizen volunteers make research less reliable
Only visual data should be trusted
questions.explanation: The final sentence describes a division of labor between rapid machine filtering and human judgment.

title: Translating More Than Words
passage: A student translation club decided to create an English version of a short Japanese story for an international school event. The sentences were not grammatically difficult, but one line caused a long debate. After receiving a small gift, a character said a common Japanese expression that literally referred to feeling sorry for the trouble. One student translated the words directly. Another argued that English readers might think the character had actually done something wrong. The group read the surrounding scene again. The character was smiling, the gift was welcome, and the relationship between the two characters was friendly. They finally chose an English phrase that expressed warm gratitude rather than literal apology. In their notes, they explained why. The experience changed the club's view of accuracy. A translation can be grammatically close to the original yet communicate the wrong social meaning. Sometimes being faithful to a text requires attention not only to dictionary definitions, but also to situation, relationship, and the effect a phrase is meant to have on a listener.
translation: 翻訳クラブは国際学校行事のため、短い日本語物語の英訳を作ることにしました。文法的には難しくありませんでしたが、ある一文をめぐって長く議論しました。小さな贈り物を受け取った登場人物が、手間をかけさせて申し訳ないという意味を文字通り含む日本語の決まり文句を言ったのです。1人は直訳しましたが、別の生徒は、英語読者には本当に悪いことをしたように聞こえるかもしれないと指摘しました。周囲の場面を読み直すと、人物は笑顔で、贈り物を喜び、2人の関係も親しいものでした。そこで最終的に、文字通りの謝罪ではなく温かい感謝を表す英語表現を選び、注記で理由を説明しました。この経験から、文法的に原文に近くても社会的な意味を誤って伝えることがあると学びました。原文に忠実であるためには、辞書の定義だけでなく、状況、関係、相手に与える効果にも注意が必要な場合があります。

questions.question: Why was the difficult line hard to translate?
choices: Its literal wording could suggest the wrong social meaning in English
The students could not read Japanese
questions.explanation: The literal apology-like wording might make English readers infer wrongdoing.

questions.question: What helped the club decide on a translation?
choices: Reading the surrounding scene and relationship
questions.explanation: Context showed that the intended effect was warm gratitude.

questions.question: What did the club finally express?
questions.explanation: They chose wording that conveyed gratitude rather than literal apology.

questions.question: How did the club's idea of accuracy change?
choices: Accuracy included conveying social meaning and intended effect
questions.explanation: The experience broadened accuracy from word matching to communicative effect.

questions.question: Which statement best matches the passage?
choices: Good translation may require moving away from literal wording
Friendly relationships should never be translated
questions.explanation: The passage argues that faithful translation sometimes requires non-literal choices.

title: When Recommendations Become Too Comfortable
passage: Recommendation systems are useful because they reduce the effort required to choose among thousands of songs, videos, books, or articles. They often learn from a user's previous behavior and offer items similar to those the user already enjoyed. This can create a pleasant experience, but a group of media researchers asked whether comfort might have a cost. In a small study, participants used two experimental news apps for three weeks. One app mainly recommended articles similar to what each participant had read before. The other did the same most of the time but deliberately inserted a limited number of high-quality articles from unfamiliar topics. Participants initially rated the second app as slightly less convenient. By the end of the study, however, they reported discovering more new interests without feeling overwhelmed. The researchers were careful not to claim that unfamiliar recommendations are always better. Too much randomness can make a system feel irrelevant, while excessive similarity can narrow what users encounter. Their conclusion was that recommendation quality should not be measured only by immediate clicks. A good system may also need to preserve opportunities for exploration, even when those opportunities are not what a user would have chosen first.
translation: 推薦システムは、何千もの曲、動画、本、記事から選ぶ手間を減らすので便利です。多くは過去の行動を学び、以前好んだものに似た項目を提示します。快適な体験になりますが、メディア研究者は、その快適さに代償があるのではないかと考えました。小規模研究で、参加者は3週間、2種類の実験的ニュースアプリを使いました。1つは過去に読んだ記事と似たものを主に推薦し、もう1つは大部分は同様ですが、限られた数の高品質な未知の分野の記事を意図的に混ぜました。最初、後者は少し不便と評価されましたが、研究終了時には、圧倒されることなく新しい関心をより多く発見したと報告しました。研究者は、未知の推薦が常に優れているとは主張していません。ランダムすぎれば無関係に感じ、似すぎれば出会う情報が狭まります。結論は、推薦の質を直近のクリックだけで測るべきではなく、最初には選ばなかった探索の機会も保つ必要があるかもしれない、というものでした。

questions.question: What question did the researchers investigate?
choices: Whether news apps should be free
Whether comfortable recommendations can limit exploration
Whether all random recommendations are useful
questions.explanation: The study examined a possible cost of recommendations that are too similar to past choices.

questions.question: How did the second app differ?
choices: It inserted some high-quality articles from unfamiliar topics
It required participants to write articles
questions.explanation: It mostly personalized normally but deliberately included limited unfamiliar content.

questions.question: How did participants' view of the second app change?
choices: They found it less convenient at first but later valued new discoveries
They immediately preferred it in every way
questions.explanation: Initial convenience ratings were lower, but later participants reported more discoveries.

questions.question: Why do the researchers reject pure randomness?
choices: It can make recommendations feel irrelevant
questions.explanation: The passage says too much randomness can make the system feel irrelevant.

questions.question: What is the central claim?
choices: Recommendation quality should include opportunities for exploration, not only immediate engagement
Users should never receive familiar content
questions.explanation: The conclusion argues for balancing relevance with exploration and measuring more than clicks.

title: Trees, Shade, and the Heat Between Buildings
passage: Cities often plant trees to reduce summer heat, but the benefits are not distributed simply according to the number of trees in a neighborhood. An environmental science class explored this issue by comparing six streets with similar traffic levels. Students measured air temperature, surface temperature, shade coverage, and the width of the space between buildings. Two streets had almost the same number of trees, yet one was noticeably cooler in the afternoon. The cooler street had larger tree canopies that shaded the pavement during the hottest hours, while buildings also blocked some late-afternoon sunlight. On the other street, young trees provided little shade and wide gaps between buildings allowed the pavement to receive direct sun for longer. The students concluded that counting trees alone could hide important differences. Their report recommended tracking canopy area and the times when shade actually falls on walking routes. It also warned against treating their six streets as proof of a universal rule; wind, building materials, and local geography could matter elsewhere. The value of the project lay less in producing a single citywide formula than in showing how a familiar policy goal—"plant more trees"—can become more precise when researchers ask what physical mechanism is expected to produce the benefit.
translation: 都市では夏の暑さを和らげるため木を植えることがありますが、恩恵は単純に地域の木の本数だけで決まりません。環境科学の授業で、交通量が似た6本の道路を比較しました。生徒たちは気温、地表温度、日陰の割合、建物間の幅を測定しました。木の本数がほぼ同じ2本の道路でも、一方は午後に明らかに涼しかったのです。涼しい道路では大きな樹冠が最も暑い時間帯に舗装面を覆い、建物も夕方の日差しを一部遮っていました。もう一方では若木の日陰が小さく、建物間の広い空間から長時間直射日光が当たっていました。生徒たちは本数だけでは重要な差を隠すと結論づけ、樹冠面積と、実際に歩道へ日陰が落ちる時間帯を記録することを提案しました。同時に、6本の道路だけで普遍的法則を証明したとは言えず、風、建材、地理も他地域では重要だと注意しました。この研究の価値は単一の都市公式を作ることより、「木を増やす」という政策目標を、どの物理的仕組みで効果が出るのか考えることで精密化した点にあります。

questions.question: Why was one of the two similarly tree-covered streets cooler?
choices: Its larger canopies and buildings provided shade at important times
questions.explanation: The cooling difference was linked to effective shade from canopies and building geometry.

questions.question: What weakness did the students identify in simply counting trees?
choices: Counts do not show how much or when shade is produced
questions.explanation: The same number of trees can provide very different canopy coverage and timing of shade.

questions.question: Why did the report mention wind and building materials?
choices: To show that the six-street result might not apply everywhere
To explain why the measurements failed
questions.explanation: The authors cautioned against overgeneralizing from a small local comparison.

questions.question: What does 'physical mechanism' refer to in the final sentence?
choices: The process through which a change is expected to create an effect
A machine used to plant trees
questions.explanation: Here it means the causal process, such as shade reducing solar heating of pavement.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly arguing?
choices: Policy goals become more useful when linked to measurable mechanisms
Every street needs the same number of trees
Young trees should never be planted
Six streets are enough to make universal rules
questions.explanation: The project refined a broad goal by connecting it to measurable shade mechanisms and limits.

title: Why Testing Can Improve Memory
passage: Students often treat a quiz as a tool that measures learning after studying is finished. Research on memory suggests that answering questions can also be part of the learning process itself. In one classroom experiment, students read a short science text. One group reread the text twice, while another group read it once and then answered questions without looking back. Immediately afterward, the rereading group performed slightly better on a test. A week later, however, the question-answering group remembered more. One explanation is that retrieving information strengthens access to it: the learner must reconstruct an idea rather than merely see it again. This does not mean every quiz automatically improves learning. Questions that are far too difficult may produce little successful retrieval, and feedback matters when students retrieve the wrong answer. Nor does the finding make reading unimportant; students need meaningful information before they can retrieve it. The practical lesson is more specific. When students already understand material reasonably well, replacing some repeated review with an attempt to recall and use the information may produce stronger long-term memory, even if that effort feels harder in the moment.
translation: 生徒は小テストを、勉強が終わった後に学習成果を測る道具と考えがちです。しかし記憶研究では、質問に答えること自体が学習過程になり得ます。ある授業実験で、生徒は短い科学文を読みました。一方の群は2回読み直し、もう一方は1回読んだ後、本文を見ずに質問へ答えました。直後のテストでは読み直し群が少し良い成績でしたが、1週間後には質問回答群の方が多く覚えていました。理由の一つは、情報を思い出そうとすることが、その情報へのアクセスを強くするからです。学習者は単に再び見るのではなく、考えを再構成しなければなりません。ただし、どんな小テストでも自動的に学習を改善するわけではありません。難しすぎれば成功した想起がほとんど起こらず、誤った答えを思い出した場合はフィードバックも重要です。また読むことが不要になるわけでもありません。十分理解した情報があって初めて想起できます。実用的な教訓は、ある程度理解した教材では、繰り返し読む一部を、思い出して使う試みに置き換えると、瞬間的には難しく感じても長期記憶を強められる可能性があるということです。

questions.question: What happened immediately after study in the experiment?
choices: The question group remembered much more
The rereading group performed slightly better
questions.explanation: The immediate result favored rereading slightly.

questions.question: What happened one week later?
choices: The rereading group still did better
questions.explanation: The delayed test showed an advantage for retrieval practice.

questions.question: Why might retrieval strengthen memory?
choices: It requires reconstructing information instead of merely seeing it
It removes the need for feedback
questions.explanation: The passage suggests reconstruction strengthens later access.

questions.question: Which limitation does the author mention?
choices: Questions that are too difficult may provide little successful retrieval
Reading before a quiz is unnecessary
Only science can be learned through retrieval
questions.explanation: The author explicitly notes difficulty and feedback as important conditions.

questions.question: What is the most accurate practical lesson?
choices: Use some retrieval practice after reasonable understanding has been built
Immediate test scores are the only useful measure
questions.explanation: The conclusion recommends replacing some repeated review, not all reading, with retrieval attempts.

title: Designing Messages for an Emergency
passage: During emergencies, public agencies must communicate quickly, but speed alone does not guarantee that a message will be useful. A coastal city learned this during a large evacuation drill. The first alert sent to residents contained detailed information about the expected storm, emergency shelters, bus changes, road closures, and several phone numbers. Everything in the message was accurate, yet interviews after the drill showed that many residents could not identify the first action they were supposed to take. Some non-native speakers also said that the long message was difficult to process under pressure. For the next drill, the city redesigned its alerts in layers. The first screen contained one short instruction—where to move and by what time—followed by a link and phone option for details. Maps used consistent symbols, and the most common instructions were prepared in several languages before the storm season began. The shorter first alert did not contain less information overall; it changed the order in which information reached people. Follow-up surveys showed better recall of the immediate action. The lesson was not that details are unimportant. Rather, in time-sensitive situations, communication must distinguish between what people need to do now and what they may need to know next.
translation: 緊急時、公的機関は素早く情報を伝える必要がありますが、速さだけで役立つメッセージになるとは限りません。沿岸都市は大規模避難訓練でそれを学びました。最初の警報には予想される嵐、避難所、バス変更、通行止め、電話番号など詳しい情報がすべて正確に入っていました。しかし訓練後の聞き取りでは、多くの住民が最初に何をすべきか答えられませんでした。また母語が英語でない住民の中には、緊張した状況で長文を処理しにくいという声もありました。次の訓練では警報を層に分けました。最初の画面には「どこへ、何時までに移動するか」という短い指示を1つ置き、その後に詳細へのリンクと電話手段を示しました。地図の記号を統一し、よく使う指示は嵐の季節前に複数言語で準備しました。最初の警報を短くしても全体情報を減らしたわけではなく、情報が届く順序を変えたのです。その後の調査では、直ちに取るべき行動の記憶が改善しました。教訓は詳細が不要ということではなく、時間が限られる状況では「今すべきこと」と「次に知る必要があること」を分ける必要があるという点でした。

questions.question: What problem did the first alert have despite being accurate?
choices: Many residents could not identify the immediate action
It was available only on paper
questions.explanation: Accuracy and detail did not make the priority action clear enough.

questions.question: How was the next alert redesigned?
